observations.body: Moses recalls the assembly at Horeb, fire, words, Ten Commandments on tablets, and his own teaching, warning Israel that they saw no form and must not make images.
observations.label: Horeb is remembered as voice without form

observations.body: Horeb is remembered as voice without form belongs to sinai remembered in the Sinai trail.
observations.label: Where this sits

observations.body: Deuteronomy 4:9–24 supplies later-memory evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: Later witnesses select and reuse Sinai in their own settings; they remain later readings rather than replacements for the Exodus event.
observations.label: Reading boundary

payload.posture: Read Deuteronomy 4:9–24 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: Horeb is remembered as voice without form belongs to the sinai remembered movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
payload.title: Horeb is remembered as voice without form
